question: Should the official Synology Chat plugin accept and stage inbound images, CSVs, and PDFs, and what retrieval, MIME, size, storage, lifetime, redirect, and private-network rules should guard that path?
rationale: Source proves the missing capability, but enabling it adds untrusted file and network ingestion to an official channel plugin, so automation should not choose the external API contract or security boundary alone.

options.title: Confirm Contract And Safe Staging
options.body: Require a redacted real Synology attachment payload or official contract, then implement bounded plugin-owned attachment staging with regression tests.

options.title: Wait For Reporter Proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until a user provides inspectable NAS webhook payloads and retrieval details so implementation does not guess fields.

options.title: Decline Bundled Expansion
options.body: Leave inbound Synology attachments unsupported unless maintainers decide the official plugin warrants the security review and maintenance cost.

recommendation.title: Confirm Contract And Safe Staging
recommendation.body: Require a redacted real Synology attachment payload or official contract, then implement bounded plugin-owned attachment staging with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest recent Synology Chat review and security-boundary context in the current history.
